property_summary: For any caller address X, calling transferOwnership(newOwner) succeeds (does not revert) iff X is the current owner — the reference enforces only the owner can transfer ownership, whereas the mutant inverts the check and allows non-owners (and prevents the owner) to perform transferOwnership for some inputs.

For all callers, transferOwnership(newOwner) succeeds iff the caller is the current owner (i.e., only owner can transfer ownership); the mutant inverts the check and lets non-owners call transferOwnership (or prevents the owner), so there exist callers for which behavior differs.

Invariant: calling transferOwnership(newOwner) succeeds (does not revert) exactly when msg.sender == owner() — the reference allows the current owner to transfer ownership; the mutant inverts the onlyOwner check and thus there exist callers for which transferOwnership succeeds on the mutant but not the reference (or vice versa).

For any caller X and any newOwner Y, after calling transferOwnership(Y) from X, the reference contract ensures owner() equals Y if and only if X was the prior owner (only the current owner can successfully change ownership); the mutant inverts the onlyOwner check so there exist some X,Y where the mutant allows a non-owner to change ownership (or prevents the owner), breaking this equivalence.

For every caller A and target newOwner N, in the correct contract a call to transferOwnership(N) can only succeed (not revert) when A is the current owner; the mutant inverts the owner check causing some non-owner A to be able to successfully change owner (or preventing the real owner) — we assert that when a call to transferOwnership succeeds, owner() equals the caller (i.e., only the caller becomes owner on success), which holds for the reference for all inputs but is violated by the mutant for some fuzzed inputs.
Only the contract owner can change the reward distributor (setRewardDistributor) — i.e., after a non-owner attempts to set it, the stored distributor remains unchanged.
